cards.text: David, Israel's king, spoke the words of this psalm (Acts 4:25). He opens with a big question about the whole world: 'Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?' Raging AND plotting is a FULL schedule, friend.

cards.question: True or false: When David says the peoples plot in vain, he means their plotting won't get them anywhere.

cards.text: The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers gather together. Biggest meeting in the world, and NOBODY brought cookies.

cards.question: The kings of the earth and the rulers take their stand together. Who are they standing against?

answers.text: The LORD and His Anointed One
Moses and the elders of Israel
Elijah and the prophets of God

cards.question: The kings and rulers are taking their stand against the LORD and His Anointed One. What do they say they want to do with Their chains and cords?

answers.text: Break them and cast them away
Gather them and hold them tight
Bury them and leave them hidden

cards.text: Here's their big plan: 'Let us break Their chains and cast away Their cords.' It's a group chat where everybody's planning to quit at once, and EVERYBODY is typing in all caps.

cards.question: The kings are plotting down on earth. Meanwhile, the One enthroned in heaven ___.

cards.text: He laughs, and the Lord taunts them. Their plan is about as believable as me telling the whole bakery I'm only eating ONE cookie today.

cards.question: True or false: After laughing at the plotting kings, God just lets their plot slide.

cards.text: Then He rebukes them in His anger, and terrifies them in His fury. And He's got something to say.

cards.question: The kings are plotting against the LORD and His Anointed One. What does God announce He has already done?

answers.text: Sent a flood over the earth

cards.text: 'I have installed My King on Zion, upon My holy mountain.' The kings want to break free, and God's King is already in place.
Then the psalm says, 'I will proclaim the decree spoken to Me by the LORD: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”'

cards.question: In the decree, the LORD tells His King, 'You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.' What does this show about the King?

answers.text: He is close to the LORD like a son
He won his crown in a great battle
He will rule for only a short time

cards.text: And the LORD isn't done. He tells the Son, 'Ask Me…' Two words, and I'm already on the edge of my gold base.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says that if the Son asks, He will make the nations the Son's inheritance and the ends of the earth His possession.

cards.text: The LORD keeps going. He tells the Son He will shatter the nations like pottery.

cards.question: The LORD says the Son will shatter the nations like pottery. What does He say the Son will break them with?

cards.text: Then the psalm turns to the kings and judges of the earth: 'Therefore be wise, O kings; be admonished, O judges of the earth.' Nothing makes you sit up straight like a sentence that starts with THEREFORE.

cards.question: The kings and judges of the earth are told to be wise. What does the psalm tell them to do next?

cards.text: They're also told to rejoice with trembling. That's me opening the oven on a brand-new cookie batch, friend: excited and SHAKING.
Then the kings get one more instruction: 'Kiss the Son…' These guys showed up to break chains, friend. THIS was not on their agenda.

cards.question: The kings are told to kiss the Son, or He may be angry and they could perish in their ___.
True or false: In the warning to the kings, the psalm says His wrath builds up slowly.
After all that warning to the kings, the psalm ends with good news. Who does it call blessed?

answers.text: All who take refuge in Him
All who rule over the earth
